themes.label: Requests to block or delete credit report items
themes.description: Consumers cite FCRA provisions and ask credit reporting agencies to block, remove or delete items they say are unauthorized or inaccurate.

examples.summary: Consumer alleges that credit reporting entities violated FCRA requirements and requests that items be blocked and removed from their credit report.
Consumer alleges that credit reporting agencies reported unauthorized and inaccurate information on the consumer's credit report and failed to block or remove the items upon request.
Consumer alleges a violation of rights under 15 USC § 1681B and requests that items be blocked and deleted from credit report.

themes.label: Disputed credit report info not corrected
themes.description: Consumers allege that disputed information, such as personal details, inquiries, or accounts, stayed on their credit file or was marked verified despite their disputes.

examples.summary: Consumer disputes accuracy of personal information appearing on credit report, claiming duplicate names, outdated addresses, and inaccurate employment information require removal or correction.
Consumer claims a credit reporting agency refused to remove disputed information from their credit report despite filing multiple disputes through letters, online submission, and phone calls.

Consumer alleges that disputed negative accounts, unauthorized hard inquiries, and incorrect address and name information remain on credit file in violation of FCRA deletion and blocking requirements.

themes.label: Debt collector disclosure and conduct concerns
themes.description: Consumers allege that debt collectors gave unclear or missing information about debts, validation, policies or payment proof, or kept contacting them after requests to stop.

examples.summary: Consumer disputes a debt and requests that a debt collector cease communications and provide written validation of the debt within 60 days.

Consumer claims to have received a collections notice for a debt of $3,900 from a debt collector but does not recognize the debt and received no explanation of its origin despite disputing the claim as potentially fraudulent.
Consumer alleges that a debt collector failed to honor a cease and desist request under the Fair Debt Collection Practices Act.

themes.label: Unclear product, loan or service terms
themes.description: Consumers allege that the terms, fees, penalties or results of a financial product or service were not clearly disclosed or were misrepresented.

examples.summary: Consumer claims a credit card account was closed while a credit protection product remained active and being charged, with inadequate disclosure of account closure reasons, product terms, benefit eligibility, and refund entitlements.
Consumer claims identity theft led to account access issues, late payment penalties, and inability to obtain debt consolidation financing needed for loan approval.

Consumer claims they were not adequately informed about early payoff penalties, lien placement on their home, solar tax credit availability, and required roof inspection before installation, leading to out-of-pocket costs when repairs became necessary.

brief.headline: Credit report dispute and disclosure complaints rise modestly, concentrated at the three credit bureaus
brief.what_is_happening: Complaints in this cluster averaged 111.0 per month over June to August 2026 versus 96.67 in the six-month baseline, a velocity of 1.141 (rank 11 of 79). Volume is choppy rather than steadily climbing, with peaks of 138 in March and 139 in June and a fall to 88 in August. In an AI-reviewed sample of 32 narratives, consumers claim items they say are unauthorized or inaccurate were not blocked or deleted (38.7%), that disputed information was not corrected (25.8%), that debt collectors gave unclear disclosures (19.4%), and that product terms were unclear (16.1%). These are unverified allegations.
brief.who_is_affected: Consumers disputing credit report items, plus a smaller group dealing with debt collectors or unclear loan and service terms. Florida accounts for 33% of complaints, followed by Texas at 11.1% and California at 8.1%. The AI sample put vulnerable-consumer signals at 3.1%, with mean severity of 3.0 out of 5.
brief.likely_root_cause: Hypothesis to test: the dispute handling and furnisher-reporting workflows may be producing responses that consumers see as unresponsive or as unclear about why items were verified or retained. This may be compounded by unclear communication of dispute outcomes, debt validation rights, and product terms. The theme mix suggests the disclosure label is largely capturing credit report dispute friction rather than product-term disclosure alone.
brief.process_or_control_to_check: Review the consumer dispute intake and investigation workflow, including how block and deletion requests are triaged, how furnisher verification responses are documented, and how outcome letters explain the result. Also check debt validation notice and cease-communication handling in collections, and plain-language review of product term disclosures.
brief.regulatory_area: Credit reporting accuracy and dispute handling, with secondary exposure in debt collection disclosure and conduct
evidence: Recent monthly average of 111.0 complaints versus a baseline average of 96.67, a velocity of 1.141 ranking 11 of 79.
TransUnion has a lift of 2.897 with 68 complaints, Equifax 2.761 with 70, and Experian 2.205 with 69, so all three are over-represented relative to their size within the product.
Resurgent Capital Services has a lift of 1.34 on 13 complaints and Encore Capital Group 1.013 on 13, only modestly above parity.
Among the other top companies, National Debt Relief (lift 0.284), Capital One (0.556), and Synchrony (0.959) are at or below parity.
0.0% of the 91 narratives in recent months were flagged as templated.
Monthly counts ranged from 65 (2025-10) to 139 (2026-06), with 88 in 2026-08, below the recent average of 111.0.
In the AI sample of 32 narratives, 38.7% sought to block or delete credit report items and 25.8% alleged disputed information was not corrected.
Florida accounts for 33% of complaints, about three times Texas at 11.1%.

checks.name: size
checks.reason: The brief ties the signal to the three bureaus, whose lifts are 2.897 (TransUnion), 2.761 (Equifax) and 2.205 (Experian), so they are over-represented well beyond their size and the attribution holds.

checks.name: templating
checks.reason: 0.0% of the 91 recent narratives were flagged as templated, far below the 30% threshold.

checks.name: concentration
checks.reason: Florida is 33% of complaints but eight states appear and 207 complaints are spread across three bureaus plus other companies, so the signal is not confined to one state or one company.

checks.name: thin_evidence
checks.reason: The AI sample has 32 complaints and there are 91 recent narratives, and the dispute-handling themes (38.7% block/delete plus 25.8% not corrected) cover about 64.5% of the sample, which supports the named root cause.

checks.name: seasonality
checks.reason: Monthly counts fell from 139 in June to 106 in July and 88 in August, so the recent average of 111.0 rests on the June peak and the latest month is about 37% below it.

skeptic.note: Rejected because the rise rests on a June peak of 139 and has fallen for two straight months to 88 in August, even though size, templating, concentration and evidence depth all pass.
